title: Void-Free Through-Glass Vias for Multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Traps
authors: Eike Iseke, Jacob Stupp, Friederike Giebel, Nila Krishnakumar, Konstantin Thronberens, Nora D. Stahr, Md. Masum Billah, Marlon Kuhn, Christian Ospelkaus
abstract: Through-substrate interconnects are a key technology for scaling surface-electrode ion traps (SEITs) toward large electrode counts and complex architectures. Dielectric substrates such as fused silica offer superior RF performance compared to silicon, but the reliable fabrication of void-free through-glass vias (TGVs) remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate a SEIT fabricated on a fused silica substrate incorporating TGVs. The via-holes are formed using Selective Laser-Induced Etching and subsequently metallized with gold by electroplating. A patent-pending geometry-assisted bottom-up plating approach enables void-free filling using constant-current electroplating without electrolyte additives or pulsed deposition schemes. Electrical characterization across multiple wafers confirms a TGV-level yield above 98.8 %, demonstrating the robustness and reproducibility of the developed TGV technology. The TGVs are combined with multilayer SEIT fabrication, enabling vertical signal routing to all electrodes while maintaining an unaffected trapping surface without wire bonds. To interface the trap with external control electronics, a glass interposer providing signal fan-out to a larger pitch is designed and fabricated. The trap chip and the interposer are integrated using thermocompression bonding, forming a compact chip-to-chip assembly. The presented technology demonstrates the first fully integrated multilayer SEIT on fused silica incorporating void-free TGVs.
summary: This paper reports a breakthrough in microfabrication for quantum hardware, demonstrating the creation of multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Traps (SEITs) on fused silica. The key innovation is a void-free, high-yield method for filling Through-Glass Vias (TGVs) using a geometry-assisted electroplating technique. This enables the complex, scalable integration of ion traps with external control electronics via a dedicated interposer.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a reliable, void-free interconnection technology to scale Surface-Electrode Ion Traps (SEITs) onto fused silica substrates.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the first fully integrated multilayer SEIT on fused silica incorporating void-free Through-Glass Vias (TGVs) with a high yield (>98.8%).
method: The process involves Selective Laser-Induced Etching (SLE) to create high-aspect-ratio vias, followed by a novel geometry-assisted bottom-up electroplating technique to ensure void-free metallization.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Trap (SEIT) fabricated on a fused silica substrate, which is integrated with a separate glass interposer chip using thermocompression bonding.
key_observables: TGV-level yield (>98.8%), mean TGV resistance ($\approx 6.6 	ext{ } \Omega$), and successful electrical connectivity across multiple wafers.
important_parameters: Via dimensions include a diameter of 75 µm and a pitch of 300 µm; the substrate material is fused silica.
main_assumptions: The success relies on the geometry-assisted bottom-up plating approach to overcome current crowding and void formation inherent in high-aspect-ratio glass vias.
figures_summary: Figures show SEM cross-sections illustrating the initial failure modes (voids, overgrowth) and the successful, uniform, void-free bottom-up filling of the TGVs. Other figures detail the final chip-to-chip bonding assembly.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for scalable SEITs on fused silica, detailing the SLE and geometry-assisted electroplating process to achieve void-free TGVs, and concluding with the full integration of the trap chip and an interposer via thermocompression bonding.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware engineering bottleneck for scaling trapped-ion quantum processors by providing a robust, high-yield interconnectivity solution (TGVs) necessary for complex, multi-electrode trap arrays.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. 3-inch fused silica wafer after Selective Laser-Induced Etching (SLE). The wafer contains 88 chips, each comprising 220 via-holes with a diameter of 75 µm.

Fig. 4. Cross-sectional SEM image of two adjacent test TGVs with a diameter of 1 mm after electroplating. Gold deposition occurs along the sidewalls, while enhanced growth at the via-hole rim (top part of the picture) leads to pronounced overgrowth caused by current crowding.
Fig. 2. SEM image of neighboring TGVs after conformal electroplating. Most TGVs exhibit pronounced overgrowth at the TGV entrance, while several remain only partially filled.

Fig. 3. Cross-sectional SEM image of a TGV after conformal electroplating. Premature closure at the via-hole entrance is observed while the lower region remains mostly unfilled, resulting in a large internal void.

Fig. 5. Cross-sectional SEM image of three neighboring via-holes after seed layer deposition. Bright contrast in the chamfer region indicates the presence of the sputtered gold seed layer, while the upper via-hole region remains uncoated. Additional notches introduced by SLE enable controlled wafer cleaving for cross-section analysis.
